title: Dependency & Supply-Chain Review (periodical run): delta vs 2026-10-23 — verify LIN-3787 (dompurify/chart.js now runtime deps) and LIN-3788 (Node 24 pin), re-triage the worsened npm advisories (1C/4H/2M) against LIN-620, provenance of 4 new lock entries
description:
## As asked

<!-- harbour-periodical-gate id="dependency-supply-chain-review" -->
**Repository:** `JKershaw/LinearViewer` (Harbour), branch `main`. **Remit:** `generateDependencySupplyChainPrompt` in `lib/periodicals.js` (registry entry `id: 'dependency-supply-chain'`, weekly cadence). **Mode:** review only. The deliverable is one committed report plus area-note edits in **one docs-only PR**. This run files **no follow-up tickets**.

**Seeded at:** LinearViewer `008d38bb0` (2026-11-10). The numbers below are a lead from that commit. Re-ground every one of them at HEAD before you use it.

---

## 0. Audit the scope before you run it

The scope below is a starting point, not a checklist. Before you run anything, look for surfaces this remit reaches that the scope does not name, and add them. For example: new runtime services reached by bare `fetch` with no npm package, the way the last run's second-read found the Resend transport; anything else that downloads at run time; and the CI image and action pins. If you could only shrink this scope, it is suspect. Search widely, but keep the output to what you find: the report has no cap and is ranked by severity (a clean, near-empty result is a real result), and area-note entries go only where a finding binds a builder or waits in an area, each note under its 6144-byte cap.

## 1. Prior runs (this review compares against them)

Reports are in `docs/reviews/`, named `dependency-supply-chain-review-YYYY-MM-DD.md`. Evidence goes in `docs/reviews/_evidence-YYYY-MM-DD[-suffix]/` when you need it.

* `dependency-supply-chain-review-2026-06-25.md`: the baseline (LIN-670, measured at `8de7da5`).
* `dependency-supply-chain-review-2026-10-23.md`: the most recent run (LIN-3786, measured at `2a26c7b1`). Read it in full. Its trend ledger gives the stable finding names to carry forward, and its running totals are what you measure against.

Report every finding as a change since 10-23: **new / unchanged / improved / worsened / resolved**. Keep the stable names from 10-23: `npm-advisories-runtime`, `vendored-dompurify-drift`, `node-runtime-eol-unpinned`, `sibling-simple-dispatcher-undici`, `resend-email-transport`, `ci-action-tag-pinning`, `lockfile-integrity`, `new-packages-this-cycle`, `mangodb-first-party-trust`, `phantom-bson-import`, `periodical-cadence-gap`. Only mint a new name for something genuinely new.

What 10-23 left open, and what has happened since (verify each item yourself):

* `vendored-dompurify-drift`**, follow-up LIN-3787 (Done,** `d81aebd2d`**).** DOMPurify is now 3.4.17. The three browser libraries are no longer committed under `public/`. They are now declared in `package.json` (`dompurify` 3.4.17 and `chart.js` 4.5.1, both pinned exact, plus the existing `marked`) and served from `node_modules` by `lib/vendor-assets.js` at the same URLs. The guard is `tests/unit/vendor-assets.test.js`. Likely **resolved**, but confirm two things: the served files match the locked versions, and nothing under `public/` still carries a stale copy.
* `node-runtime-eol-unpinned`**, follow-up LIN-3788 (Done,** `6d51e61e5`**).** `engines.node: "24"` and `.nvmrc` = `24` are in place. CI reads `node-version-file: '.nvmrc'`. The guard is `tests/unit/node-version-pin.test.js`. Check whether the production builder (Railway) actually honours this. The source cannot prove it; the 10-23 run left it open.
* `npm-advisories-runtime`**, tracked by LIN-620 (still Backlog, list stale).** A seeding-time `npm audit` still shows **7 packages, but now 1C/4H/2M** (10-23: 1C/3H/3M): `body-parser`, `express`, `express-rate-limit`, `ip-address`, `path-to-regexp`, `proxy-addr`, `qs`. That looks **worsened**. Find which package escalated. Redo the reachability triage against the live call sites, using 10-23's table as the template: hop-count `trust proxy` in `server.js`, the IP-keyed limiters in `routes/`, and the parser limits. Is the production `req.ip` `::ffff:`-mapped? That question is still unverified at the edge. Reconcile against LIN-620's list again, but do not duplicate it.
* `sibling-simple-dispatcher-undici`**.** The sibling `JKershaw/simple-dispatcher` still locks `undici@7.28.0`, which it imports in `opencode-runner.js`. LIN-1456 is Done, so that repo now has CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`). Read it only; do not edit the sibling repo.
* `ci-action-tag-pinning`**.** Still tag-pinned at seeding: `actions/checkout@v4`, `setup-node@v4`, `upload-artifact@v4`, and the images `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.57.0-noble` and `mongo:8.0.32`. Is there still no `permissions:` block?
* `mangodb-first-party-trust` (still `^0.1.2`; were 0.1.3/0.1.4 adopted?), `phantom-bson-import` (`scripts/lin3014/capture-kpis.mjs`), and `periodical-cadence-gap` (10-23 to today is about 18 days against a weekly cadence).

## 2. The ecosystem you are reviewing

* **npm**, `"type": "module"`. The manifest is `package.json` and the committed lockfile is `package-lock.json`. There is no build step. Railway deploys it.
* **Runtime set (12 at seeding):** `@jkershaw/mangodb` (first-party), `chart.js`, `dompurify`, `dotenv`, `express`, `express-rate-limit`, `express-session`, `graphql`, `graphql-request`, `https-proxy-agent`, `marked`, `mongodb`. **Dev (4):** `@playwright/test`, `playwright`, `acorn`, `acorn-walk`.
* **Browser libraries:** these used to be committed files. They now come from `node_modules` through `lib/vendor-assets.js`. That is a change to the minimal-runtime posture: it trades committed copies (no audit coverage) for 2 new declared runtime deps. Judge whether LIN-3787 justified that trade, and whether it was correct.
* **Self-hosted non-JS assets:** `public/fonts/` (woff2). Licensing belongs to LIN-1651; mention it only if provenance changed.
* **Lockfile delta** `2a26c7b1..HEAD` **at seeding:** +4 entries, `chart.js`, `dompurify`, `@kurkle/color` (from chart.js) and `@types/trusted-types` (from dompurify, check whether it is optional or runtime). Nothing removed. 109 → 113 entries. `npm audit` metadata: prod 106 / dev 6 / optional 2.
* Existing dependency guards to read: `tests/unit/lin-688-undici-not-a-dependency.test.js`, `tests/unit/vendor-assets.test.js`, `tests/unit/node-version-pin.test.js`.

## 3. Run the review

Every finding must rest on the live manifest, the lockfile and the resolved tree at HEAD. Use only the tools npm already provides. Add **no new scanner dependency**, and do **not** run `npm audit fix`, `npm update` or any install that rewrites the lockfile.

* **Known CVEs:** `npm audit --json` and `--omit=dev`. Count packages and advisories separately, and label each. Rank by whether the vulnerable path can be reached from this project's own code, not by the raw count.
* **Lockfile integrity:** `npm ci --dry-run`; `npm ls --all`; `npm audit signatures`. Use `jq` over the lockfile to find non-registry `resolved` URLs, missing `integrity`, nested duplicates (10-23 found 7), and entries a clean install would not produce.
* **New packages since** `2a26c7b1`**:** for each of the 4 above, record registry first-publish date and age, weekly downloads, maintainers, repository, whether lock integrity matches `npm view`, and how close the name sits to a popular package (typosquatting or slopsquatting).
* **Tree growth:** compare 107 → 108 → 113 resolved packages over time, and say where the growth sits.
* **Runtime services with no npm package:** the Resend transport (`lib/email-transport.js`) and anything new that calls out with bare `fetch`. Look at service trust only at this altitude.
* These classes are **a floor, not a ceiling**. Find the complete set for this remit from the repo.

## 4. Defend the minimal-runtime posture

Every runtime dependency added since the last run is a finding that must be justified. Name it, give its provenance, and say why a built-in or committed alternative would not do. This cycle that means `dompurify` **and** `chart.js`, plus any transitive runtime package they pulled in. A new dev-only dependency is lower stakes but still gets noted.

## 5. Altitude: do not flag what another review owns

This review covers supply chain and provenance. The **Security Review** owns generic CVE scope. Its next run is **LIN-4411** (Backlog, delta vs 2026-10-23), and its 10-23 report deferred `npm audit` and the vendored libraries to *this* review. Use the audit only as the baseline that frames your work. The findings that belong to this review alone are lockfile drift, name proximity, the growth trend, unjustified runtime additions, and runtime and CI provenance. If something sits in the gap between reviews and no review owns it (for example CI action pinning, or the production Node line), it is in scope here.

## 6. The report

Write `docs/reviews/dependency-supply-chain-review-<run date>.md`. Use the 10-23 report's structure: instruments, re-grounding table, findings ranked by severity, then a **Trend Ledger** (stable name / severity / delta) and **Running totals** (resolved packages, lockfile entries, direct runtime/dev deps, new packages this cycle, open CVEs as packages and advisories, full tree and `--omit=dev`, non-registry/missing-integrity count, browser libs and their versions). Add a final `## Adversarial Second-Read` section (§9). Do not pad the report and do not cap it.

## 7. Area notes (file no follow-up tickets)

The registry is `docs/areas/areas.json` (first match wins). The rules are in `docs/areas/README.md`. The guard is `tests/unit/area-notes.test.js` (6144-byte cap per note; a Waiting entry's first cited path must map to that note's area; every cited path must exist; no line numbers). The leftover rule is `LEFTOVER_RULE` in `lib/prompts/leftover-words.js`.

* Start with `git diff --name-only 2a26c7b1..HEAD` and map each changed file to its area, so you look first where work landed.
* Likely homes: `lib/vendor-assets.js` → platform-and-plumbing; `server.js` (trust proxy) → wiring; `routes/proxy*.js` limiters → agent-api, and other `routes/` limiters → web-routes; `lib/email-transport.js` → auth-accounts-and-workspaces; `public/common.js` (sanitiser call) → front-end-browser; `lib/security-headers.js` → front-end-pages.
* **Watch the cap:** `llm-and-prompts.md` and `runs-and-dispatch.md` are already within a few bytes of 6144 (6139 and 6140 at seeding). If you touch one, prune it.
* In each note you touch, prune entries that are settled or no longer true.
* Add a **Waiting** entry when a finding leaves work in an area. Add a **Lesson** when it is a rule builders there must follow. Each entry cites the area's file first, then names this reading as its source: "(Dependency & Supply-Chain Review, <run date>)", with the report path as the second cited path.
* A finding already ticketed (for example anything on LIN-620) stays in the report only, never in a note too.
* **Findings with no area file to cite go only in the closing comment, addressed to the person, never in a ticket:** `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `.github/workflows/*`, `.nvmrc`, and the sibling repo.
* A larger tidy becomes a Waiting entry worded as a size of move, and is also listed for the person.
* A cross-area seam goes under the area where a change would start, naming the other side. Say plainly in the report that seams have no full home in the notes yet.

**PR:** make a branch named like `chore/<this-ticket-id>-dependency-review`. One docs-only commit holds the report, any evidence directory, and the note edits. Rebase it onto `main`, then get it green under `tests/unit/area-notes.test.js` and the required checks (`.github/workflows/test.yml`). **Do not merge it.**

## 8. Review only

Change no code, dependencies, config or secrets, and no docs beyond the report, its evidence and the note edits. Run no auto-fix that rewrites the manifest or lockfile. Any fix goes in the report as a finding for the person. An operator instruction not to touch files applies to the code under review, not to this deliverable.

## 9. Adversarial second-read (required before hand-off)

Once the report and note edits are written, a genuinely separate reader must answer, cold: *"what is the largest item in this window that this report missed or misfiled?"*

* **Tier 1** (preferred): a wholly separate session.
* **Tier 2** (accepted): a fresh-context sub-agent with no memory of the turn that wrote the report.
* Tier 3 (this session re-reading its own report) is **not accepted**.

Post **one** comment on this task that holds all three of these lines, plus the tier you used:

* `Adversarial second-read verdict: AGREE` or `Adversarial second-read verdict: DISAGREE`
* `Differed from top finding: YES` or `Differed from top finding: NO`
* `Disposition: fixed in place`, `Disposition: escalated` or `Disposition: no change`

Copy the same lines into the report's `## Adversarial Second-Read` section, together with the tier, the question and the reader's answer in full. AGREE and DISAGREE both go on to the normal hand-off. A DISAGREE verdict is itself the escalation.

## 10. Hand-off (do not merge, do not set Done)

1. As soon as the PR is open, post its **full URL** as a comment on this task.
2. Post the second-read comment (§9).
3. Post a **closing comment**: a concise summary ranked by severity, with a link to the report. It names the PR, lists any larger tidy and every finding with no area file to cite, and says who finishes: **review approves, then close-out merges the PR, sets this task to Done and posts the final summary.** If the PR cannot be made green, name what blocks it.

Leave the task **In Progress**. This run stops at the hand-off.

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Size of the move

**Size:** just the task
**Why:** One docs-only review report plus area-note edits, measured against the 10-23 run; every lead in the ask still holds at the seeded commit and nothing found binds this review to a wider change.
**Cuts:** none
**Decided by:** the standing policy

## Close-out stub (research findings and plan, discharged)

Implemented: the dependency & supply-chain review report `docs/reviews/dependency-supply-chain-review-2026-11-10.md`, with 2 evidence files and area-note entries in `docs/areas/platform-and-plumbing.md` and `docs/areas/wiring.md`. Merged in PR [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2393](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2393>) as `4d23fa158` (CI green on `05155c44e`). The plan was implemented as approved; the only deviations are the review's three accuracy fixes in the report (incident-record provenance, `qs` reachability reason, Node 24 spike and CI row), made at close-out. The full research findings and plan are preserved in the task snapshots and the comment trail. Open for a person (not filed, per the ask): the Railway Node line and production `req.ip` checks, the Harbour GitHub App check for 20-23 Oct, and `EMAIL_TRANSPORT=off`; the remedy for the worsened advisories is LIN-620.

## Implementation Plan

Implemented as approved (see the stub above).

**Session fit:** fits one session.

comments.body:
## Research notes — LIN-4412 (Dependency & Supply-Chain Review, 2026-11-10)

**Grounding:** LinearViewer HEAD = `origin/main` = `008d38bb0` (the seeded commit; nothing landed after the ticket was created at 13:16Z, so the re-ground check is trivially clean). Sibling `JKershaw/simple-dispatcher` at `5d8489e` (read only). Instruments ran on local Node 25.9.0 / npm 11.12.1. **Nothing in either repo was modified.** No lockfile-rewriting command touched the repo; the one `npm install --package-lock-only` ran on a scratch copy of `package.json` + `package-lock.json`.

This is the research stage, so it delivers measurements and a plan. The report, note edits, PR, second-read and hand-off (§6–§10 of the ask) belong to the implementation stage. Nothing is cut; see "Recommended approach".

### Instruments (all at `008d38bb0`)

| Instrument | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm audit --json` | **7 packages (1C/4H/2M)** · **15 advisories (1C/4H/8M/2L)**; metadata prod 106 / dev 6 / optional 2 / total 112 |
| `npm audit --omit=dev --json` | identical to the full tree |
| `npm ci --dry-run` | exit 0, "up to date" |
| `npm ls --all` | exit 0. UNMET entries are optional only: the 7 optional peers of `mongodb`, plus `encoding` under `graphql-request → cross-fetch → node-fetch` (pre-existing, optional; the 10-23 report did not list it) |
| `npm audit signatures` | **112/112 verified**, 9 with attestations |
| `jq` over lockfile | 113 entries (incl. root); 0 non-`registry.npmjs.org` resolved; 0 missing integrity; the same 7 nested dedups as 10-23 |
| Lock regen on a scratch copy | the only diff is that the lock root lacks `"engines": {"node": "24"}`. LIN-3788 edited `package.json` without refreshing the lock root |
| `npm pack` + sha256 of upstream tarballs | served files are byte-identical to `dompurify@3.4.17`, `marked@17.0.1` and `chart.js@4.5.1` |
| `npm view` / npm downloads API / `gh api /advisories` | provenance of the 4 new entries; advisory text |
| Spike: GHSA-27r3 against the locked express 4.22.1 / body-parser 1.20.4 | see F1 |
| Guards: `area-notes`, `vendor-assets`, `node-version-pin`, `lin-688-undici-not-a-dependency` | 29/29 pass at HEAD |

### Re-grounding the leads

| Lead in the ask | Live | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| 7 pkgs, 1C/4H/2M | 7 pkgs, 1C/4H/2M | ✓ |
| "which package escalated?" | **`body-parser`**: new high **GHSA-27r3-jxmh-p828**, published **2026-10-23T20:53Z**, hours after the 10-23 run measured | answered |
| advisories (10-23: 13 = 1C/3H/7M/2L) | **15 = 1C/4H/8M/2L**: +GHSA-27r3 (body-parser, H), +GHSA-6pq8-jhm2-2vcw (qs, M) | worsened |
| lock 109 → 113, +4 entries | ✓: `chart.js`, `dompurify`, `@kurkle/color`, `@types/trusted-types`; nothing removed | ✓ |
| "107 → 108 → 113 resolved packages" | **corrected: 107 → 108 → 112 resolved** (113 lock entries includes the root) | ✗ lead corrected |
| `@types/trusted-types` optional or runtime? | `"optional": true` (dompurify `optionalDependencies`); type definitions only, no executable code | answered |
| 12 runtime / 4 dev | ✓ | ✓ |
| `trust proxy` hop-count | `app.set('trust proxy', 1)`, production only (`server.js`, moved from the 10-23 line) | ✓ |
| parser limits (10-23 cited 250kb / 14mb / 12mb literals) | reshaped: global `express.json({limit:'250kb'})` + `express.urlencoded`; route-scoped `json({type:'text/plain', limit: FEEDBACK_BODY_LIMIT})` in `routes/workspace-api-feedback.js` and `json({type:()=>true, limit: ATTACHMENT_UPLOAD_BODY_LIMIT})` in `routes/proxy-writes.js` (computed numeric limits, valid); test-only 4mb seed parser and `routes/test.js` | template updated |
| CI pins: checkout/setup-node/upload-artifact @v4, playwright v1.57.0-noble, mongo:8.0.32; no `permissions:` | ✓ all unchanged; still no `permissions:` in `test.yml` or `secret-scan-scheduled.yml` | ✓ |
| mangodb `^0.1.2`, 0.1.3/0.1.4 adopted? | still locked 0.1.2; 0.1.3 (2026-01-21) and 0.1.4 (2026-01-31) not adopted | ✓ |
| sibling undici 7.28.0 | ✓ still locked; **now 23 advisories (7H/13M/3L)**, was 15 (3H); fix ≥7.30.1 | worsened |

### Per-layer audit (each claim checked against source)

**L1 · Manifest + lockfile** (`package.json`, `package-lock.json`). Runtime set of 12 is as the ask states. `dompurify` and `chart.js` are exact-pinned, added by `d81aebd2d` (LIN-3787); `engines.node: "24"` came from `6d51e61e5` (LIN-3788). Lock is v3. All entries come from the registry with integrity. The only drift: the root entry lacks `engines` (a clean regen adds it). `npm ci` does not check this, so it is cosmetic. Still, it is an entry a clean install would produce differently. → `lockfile-integrity` unchanged (clean), plus one Info note.

**L2 · Browser-lib serving** (`lib/vendor-assets.js`, mounted in `server.js` before `express.static('public')`). `VENDOR_ASSETS` maps `/purify.min.js` to `dompurify/dist/purify.min.js`, `/marked.min.js` to `marked/lib/marked.umd.js`, and `/chart.umd.min.js` to `chart.js/dist/chart.umd.min.js`. Each is `statSync`ed at boot. Served bytes: DOMPurify sha256 `cd37898f9782adf5` (banner 3.4.17). marked `e131975cfd9e6fd1` and Chart.js `48444a82d4edcb5b` are **the same bytes the old vendored files had** (10-23 table), so only DOMPurify's bytes changed. `git ls-files public` has no copy of any of the three (`public/chart-helpers.js` is app code). The `prototypes/lin-1412-chat/shape-{a,b}.html` script tags now point at `../../node_modules/...` (dev-only prototypes). Guard `tests/unit/vendor-assets.test.js` passes. **New sub-finding:** `chart.umd.min.js` inlines `@kurkle/color v0.3.2`, while the lock installs `@kurkle/color@0.3.4`. The installed copy is never executed: no server import of chart.js, and the browser gets the inlined copy. So `npm audit` watches the declared transitive package, not the code actually served. This is a narrow but real blind spot in "under audit coverage".

**L3 · Node runtime line** (`.nvmrc` = `24`, `engines.node` = `"24"`, every `setup-node` step uses `node-version-file: '.nvmrc'`; guard `tests/unit/node-version-pin.test.js`). Railpack's documented resolution order (railpack.com/languages/node): `RAILPACK_NODE_VERSION` env, then `devEngines.runtime`, then **`engines.node`**, then `.nvmrc`, then `.node-version`, then mise; the default is `lts`. So the pin is honoured **if** the service builds with Railpack and no `RAILPACK_NODE_VERSION` override is set. Both facts live in Railway service settings, not in the repo: no `railway.json`/`nixpacks.toml`/`Dockerfile`/`Procfile` (the platform-and-plumbing note already records "no deploy job or Railway config in the repository"). `process.version` is still only in a server-side error log (`lib/linear-fetch.js`), and `/health` returns `{status:'ok'}`. **Still unverified at runtime; improved in source.**

**L4 · Request parsing + `npm-advisories-runtime` reachability** (`server.js`, `routes/*`).

| Package@locked | Worst advisory | Delta vs 10-23 | Reachability at HEAD |
|---|---|---|---|
| `body-parser@1.20.4` | **GHSA-27r3** high: trailing bytes after a compressed body re-thrown as an uncaught exception, "terminates the process", pre-auth, before routing | **new, the escalation** | **Code path reachable.** Every app parser uses default `inflate: true`: the global `express.urlencoded` + `express.json({limit:'250kb'})` mounted before session and routes, plus the two route-scoped `json()` parsers. **Process termination is absorbed by the `process.on('uncaughtException', …)` backstop in `server.js`**, which logs and keeps the process alive. Spike (scratchpad `bp.mjs`/`bp2.mjs`, the repo's own express from `node_modules`): gzip, deflate and br payloads with trailing bytes, sent in one write and in split writes, with and without the backstop, on **Node 25.9**. gzip → 400, deflate → 200, br → 415; the process **never died, even with no backstop**. So the naive PoC did not reproduce; Node 24 (the prod line) was not available locally. No first-party client sends compressed bodies (grep: only `lib/runner-kit/broker.mjs`, which strips `content-encoding`), so the advisory's `inflate:false` workaround would be safe. Effective: **Medium**, the only advisory with a reachable path. |
| `proxy-addr@2.0.7` | GHSA-jqcg critical | unchanged | Not reachable: hop-count `trust proxy 1`, no subnet trust |
| `express-rate-limit@8.2.1` | GHSA-46wh high | unchanged, **exposure narrowed** | Conditional on prod `req.ip` being `::ffff:`-mapped (**still unverified at the edge**). 10 IP-keyed limiters, reshaped: `routes/dispatch.js` ×4 (default key); `routes/proxy.js` `proxyTokenCreationLimiter` (default key), `defaultCopyTokenCreationLimiter` (account, else `ipKeyGenerator`) and `proxyLimiter`, now keyed per **proven credential** and falling back to IP only for unproven tokens (LIN-4378, `f7d1923e6`, 2026-11-08); `routes/email-auth.js` (sign-in); `routes/task-mode.js`; `routes/workspace-api-feedback.js` `feedbackSubmitLimiter` (account, else IP; moved out of `workspace-api.js`). The `proxy-flight-companion.js` limiters key on token/urlKey and are unaffected |
| `ip-address@10.0.1` | GHSA-mwp4 high (6 advisories) | unchanged | Low: sole consumer is `ipKeyGenerator(req.ip)` |
| `path-to-regexp@0.1.12` | GHSA-37ch high | unchanged | Not reachable: a grep for two `:params` in one segment across `routes/` and `server.js` returns nothing |
| `qs@6.14.1` | 4 advisories (3M/1L), **+GHSA-6pq8 new** (`stringify` with `arrayFormat:'comma'`) | worsened (count) | Not reachable: the app never imports `qs` or calls `stringify`; `urlencoded` is `extended:false` |
| `express@4.22.1` | rollup | unchanged | n/a |

All are fixable in range (`fixAvailable: true`). body-parser 1.20.9 satisfies express 4.22.x's `~1.20.x` range, so LIN-620's non-breaking lock refresh still clears everything.

**L5 · LIN-620 reconciliation.** Still Backlog. Its last comment (10-23) already added proxy-addr and body-parser. This run adds two items: body-parser is now **high with a reachable code path** (GHSA-27r3), and qs has gained GHSA-6pq8. Per the ask: reconcile, do not duplicate. The implementation stage should post one short comment on LIN-620 (not a new ticket) and keep the item out of the area notes.

**L6 · New packages this cycle** (all integrity strings equal `npm view dist.integrity`):

| | `dompurify@3.4.17` | `chart.js@4.5.1` | `@kurkle/color@0.3.4` | `@types/trusted-types@2.0.7` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kind | direct runtime, exact | direct runtime, exact | transitive runtime (chart.js `^0.3.0`) | transitive **optional** (dompurify optionalDeps) |
